title: Harden the launcher: no working-directory bunfig.toml or .env before Ward runs
description: Found in review of PR #1 (WCLI-2). Ward launched through `bun` reads the current directory's bunfig.toml and .env before main.ts runs: a planted preload executes arbitrary code with argv in reach, a malformed bunfig.toml is echoed to stderr, and .env is loaded into process.env. Ward runs inside repositories an agent can edit, so this is the product's trust boundary, not a dev nuisance. Ship a compiled launcher built with --no-compile-autoload-dotenv and --no-compile-autoload-bunfig (tsconfig and package.json autoload are already off by default) and never advertise a bun-shebang entry.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The shipped ward binary is built with bunfig and .env autoload disabled, and package.json bin resolves to it, not to TypeScript source

A test runs the packaged binary in a directory containing a bunfig.toml preload that throws with argv and a .env defining a sentinel: the preload never runs, no sentinel reaches stdout/stderr, and process.env lacks the .env key
Positive control: the same test run against `bun src/cli/main.ts` fails

implementationNotes: Delivered in PR #8. Measured on bun 1.3.14 (macOS arm64 locally; Linux ARM64 in CI run 36380579242): the default 'bun build --compile' ALSO loads the working directory's bunfig.toml and .env, so the flags are required, not belt-and-braces. The four --no-compile-autoload-* flags live in scripts/build.ts; package.json bin.ward = dist/ward. The .env half of AC2 is measured by a probe compiled through the same buildExecutable, since Ward prints no environment. AC3 names 'bun src/cli/main.ts', but main.ts only exports runWard and launches nothing; the controls run 'bun src/cli/ward.ts', the actual entry, which is what the criterion means. Independent review (opum-workflow reviewer) found nothing at critical, high or medium, and five lows. Fixed here: L1, the flag test now asserts the argv buildCommand returns, not the list constant. L2, a malformed-bunfig case with its control. L4, the non-disclosure entry-point cases now run the packaged executable via test/support/packaged.ts. Also a temp-dir leak on a failed build. Recorded rather than fixed: L3 (above) and L5, nothing builds dist/ward itself in CI; when release packaging lands, CI should build through 'bun run build' and run one hostile-directory check on that artifact. Positive controls, each planted and then reverted: dropping the bunfig flag fails 5 of 10 launcher tests, dropping the dotenv flag fails 3, and a buildCommand that omits the flag list fails 6. Out of scope, filed as WCLI-19: inherited BUN_OPTIONS and BUN_BE_BUN still reach the executable.
finalSummary: Ward now ships only as a compiled executable (scripts/build.ts, bun run build -> dist/ward, package.json bin) built with dotenv, bunfig, tsconfig and package.json autoload off, so a repository's bunfig.toml preload, a malformed bunfig and .env no longer run or load before Ward's code. Verified by test/launcher.test.ts: every hostile-directory check runs against the packaged executable and against a bun-launched control that must detect the plant. Planted-regression runs show the tests fail without each flag. bun run check passes 61/61, and PR #8's CI run 36380579242 passed on Linux ARM64. The inherited BUN_OPTIONS and BUN_BE_BUN are not closed by any build flag and are tracked as WCLI-19, which depends on WCLI-3.
